content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Incident Response Lifecycle (NIST and SANS)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"A structured Incident Response (IR) lifecycle is crucial for any organization looking to minimize the impact of cyber security breaches. Two of the most widely adopted frameworks are provided by NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) in SP 800-61 and SANS."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 1: Preparation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Preparation involves equipping the organization to handle potential incidents before they occur. This phase ensures that tools, policies, and personnel are ready to respond at a moment's notice."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Establishing an Incident Response Plan (IRP) and defining roles and responsibilities."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Deploying monitoring tools like SIEM, EDR, and network intrusion detection systems."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Conducting regular training and tabletop exercises for the response team."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 2: Identification (Detection and Analysis)"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Identification focuses on detecting deviations from normal operations and determining whether an incident has occurred. Analysts must gather logs, review alerts, and scope the potential impact."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"grep -i 'failed password' /var/log/auth.log | awk '{print $1, $2, $3, $11}' | sort | uniq -c"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 3: Containment, Eradication, and Recovery"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once an incident is identified, the immediate goal is containment to prevent further spread. Eradication removes the threat components (such as malware or unauthorized accounts), and recovery restores systems back to standard operating status."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Short-term containment: Isolating compromised hosts from the network."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Long-term containment: Applying temporary architectural fixes while rebuilding systems."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Eradication: Removing malware binaries, closing exploited vulnerabilities, and resetting compromised credentials."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Recovery: Restoring clean data from backups and validating system integrity."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 4: Lessons Learned (Post-Incident Activity)"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"The final phase ensures that the organization learns from the event. A post-mortem meeting should be held to document what happened, what went well, and what needs improvement."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Completing a comprehensive incident report with a detailed timeline."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Updating defensive controls and security policies to prevent recurrence."}]
